ingredients.cook_qty: 6 tbsp, plus more for the table

instructions: Bring a large pot of water to a boil.
Meanwhile, grate the 2 garlic cloves into a medium bowl. Add the chili oil with its chili crisp, soy sauce, black vinegar and sugar. Stir until the sugar dissolves.
Thinly slice the scallions and chop the cilantro.

Add the wontons to the boiling water in two batches and lower the heat to a gentle simmer. Cook for 3 to 4 minutes, until they float and the wrappers look see-through. Frozen wontons take a minute or two longer.
Transfer the wontons into the bowl with a slotted spoon. Add 4 tbsp of the hot cooking water and toss until they are coated.
Spoon the wontons and sauce into 4 bowls and top with the scallions and cilantro.
Serve with extra chili oil on the table for the adults.
method_notes: No version had 20 ratings. Omnivore's Cookbook (4.95 from 19) leads: boil, then toss in chili oil, black vinegar, sweet soy and grated garlic, with a little of the cooking water. Food Network Kitchen has no rating but gives the plain sauce used here (6 tbsp chili oil, 1/4 cup light soy, black vinegar, garlic, 1 tsp sugar). Both make their own wontons and chili oil; this uses frozen wontons and a jarred chili oil as the list asks. The soy is cut to 3 tbsp and the vinegar raised for balance.
